segments.note: Chartered in 1882 as the Louisville, Henderson and Texas Railway, nicknamed 'The Texas Line' for its ambition to eventually reach Texas via St. Louis. The first train ran between Owensboro and Stephensport in 1888, part of a line that would ultimately run 136+ miles from Louisville through Irvington, Stephensport, Fordsville, and Owensboro to Henderson on the Ohio River (from which L&N trackage rights reached Evansville, Indiana, and 166 more miles of connecting track reached St. Louis). The company went bankrupt in the 1890s. Frequency for this era is estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Reorganized out of bankruptcy as the Louisville, Henderson and St. Louis Railway in 1896. By the early 20th century the line ran eight trains daily. The Louisville and Nashville Railroad purchased the company in 1929.

segments.note: Operated as an L&N branch from 1929; passenger service declined through the mid-20th century, in line with the national contraction of branch-line passenger trains, ending altogether in 1958. Frequency for this era is estimated, unsourced. The route survives today as CSX's freight-only LH&StL Subdivision, one of the few Kentucky branches in this dataset that lost its passenger service well before Amtrak's 1971 creation.
